body:
Undocumented public constant


All language items that are publicly exposed must be documented. Providing documentation through comments or the `#[doc]` attribute allows other developers to conveniently understand the code and use the modules or crates appropriately. Contrary to `rustdoc`, this issue is also raised on all non-private items. If an item has been marked `pub`, `pub(crate)`, or `pub(path)`, it indicates the possibility of usage outside the same module, and hence would ideally require documentation, despite not being exposed outside the crate.

**issue (bug_risk):** Glossary-term persistence failures are caught and discarded, so `saveCorrectedTranscript` returns successfully with an empty `learnedTerms` list and the UI shows "Transcript updated" even when every dictionary insert failed. The user is told the correction succeeded but is not told that auto-learning failed.

**Triggers:** When the transcript update succeeds but a glossary-term insert fails.

**Suggested fix:** Return or throw a dictionary-persistence error separately from transcript saving, and show an explicit failure or partial-success toast when auto-learning cannot persist a term.

✅ Addressed in dcca411114314ed649a94dba2e1f17dd872ce7e7: Glossary insertion failures are now counted and returned as failedTerms, and the UI displays explicit partial-success or failure feedback instead of only saying the transcript was updated.

**nitpick:** The function documentation says it adds "the corrected words" to glossary terms, but the implementation deliberately adds only tokens beginning with an uppercase letter and skips ordinary lowercase corrections. The public action contract therefore overstates what auto-learning does.

**Triggers:** When callers rely on the action docstring to expect ordinary corrected words to be learned.

**Suggested fix:** Document that only capitalized proper-noun-like tokens are learned, matching `extractAutoLearnTerms` and the actual behavior.

```suggestion
 * Persists a user's manual correction to a transcription's final text and,
 * when auto-learn is enabled, adds only corrected tokens beginning with an
 * uppercase letter as proper-noun-like glossary terms.
```

✅ Addressed in dcca411114314ed649a94dba2e1f17dd872ce7e7: The documentation now accurately states that auto-learning adds only corrected tokens beginning with an uppercase letter as proper-noun-like glossary terms.

body:
**WARNING:** Untranslated i18n strings in non-English locales.

The five new keys (`added_count_words_to_your_dictionary`, `added_term_to_your_dictionary`, `auto_learn_dictionary`, `transcript_updated`, `when_you_correct_a_transcription_add_the_corrected_names_and`) are added with English values in all 10 non-English locales (de, es, fr, it, ko, pt, pt-BR, zh-CN, zh-TW). Users on those locales will see English strings until translations land. The PR description claims `pnpm --filter desktop i18n` extracted and synchronized messages, but the result is English fallbacks as the only copy. Either stub-translate each locale or land translations in the same PR before merge.

---
Reply with `@kilocode-bot fix it` to have Kilo Code address this issue.

**SUGGESTION:** Trailing whitespace after the semicolon on this line.

The new line is `handsFreeDelayMs?: number | null; ` with a trailing space. `pnpm --filter desktop lint` runs prettier in check mode, and trailing spaces typically fail format checks. Note also that the line above (1143) has a pre-existing trailing space; both should be cleaned. Re-running `pnpm gen:bindings` would also regenerate this file from the Rust source of truth instead of hand-editing it (the PR description acknowledges that was not run).

diff_hunk:
@@ -0,0 +1,325 @@
+/**
+ * Extracts the words a user corrected while editing a dictation result, so
+ * mausVoice can learn them as glossary terms.
+ *
+ * The engine is intentionally conservative. It only learns a token when it is
+ * new in the corrected text (it did not appear in the original), looks like a
+ * proper noun (an initial capital letter), and is not already a dictionary
+ * term. A large edit is treated as a rewrite and learns nothing.
+ */
+
+const MIN_TERM_LENGTH = 2;
body:
**SUGGESTION:** `MIN_TERM_LENGTH = 2` silently drops legitimate short proper nouns.

A correction of "S" to "T" or a two-letter name like "Jo" to "Bo" is ignored. The function targets proper nouns, so the floor is presumably conservative, but the unit tests do not cover the boundary, and the JSDoc does not call out the limitation. Either lower the floor to 1 and rely on the uppercase + common-word filters, or document the two-character minimum so users do not expect short names to be learned.

---
Reply with `@kilocode-bot fix it` to have Kilo Code address this issue.

**SUGGESTION:** No early return when the draft equals the current transcript.

If the user opens Edit and clicks Save without changing anything, `saveCorrectedTranscript` still persists the same text and runs the full glossary extraction pipeline. Add a guard like `if (finalDraft.trim() === finalTranscriptText) { setIsEditingFinal(false); return; }` to avoid a needless DB round-trip and a misleading toast.

---
Reply with `@kilocode-bot fix it` to have Kilo Code address this issue.

**SUGGESTION:** Comment the intent around the partial-failure swallow.

`createGlossaryTerms` in `dictionary.actions.ts` is intentionally non-throwing: it logs and continues. That means the catch block here only ever fires for `updateTranscription` failures; the glossary call at line 54 cannot throw. A future maintainer reading this code may try to "fix" the missing throw or wrap `learnTermsFromCorrection` in a try/catch that never fires. A one-line comment noting that glossary-creation errors are absorbed by `createGlossaryTerms` and reflected in the toast count would prevent that.

---
Reply with `@kilocode-bot fix it` to have Kilo Code address this issue.

**SUGGESTION:** `Object.values(state.termById).flatMap((term) => [term.sourceValue, term.destinationValue])` includes an empty string for every non-replacement glossary term because `destinationValue` is `""`. The downstream `.filter(Boolean)` in `extractAutoLearnTerms` drops them, so behavior is correct, but the call site is doing more work than needed and the intent is hidden. Skip empty `destinationValue` entries at the call site, or document that glossary terms always have an empty `destinationValue` so the flatMap is expected.

---
Reply with `@kilocode-bot fix it` to have Kilo Code address this issue.

**SUGGESTION:** Trailing whitespace after the semicolon is still present on this line. This file is regenerated by `pnpm gen:bindings` from the Rust command signatures, so the trailing space must be removed in the source generator, not edited in the generated output. The previous review already flagged this; it has not been fixed.

body:
**WARNING:** The new i18n key is malformed. `added_added_words_to_your_dictionary_failed_failed` is a concatenation of two intended keys (`added_words_to_your_dictionary` and `added_failed`) and embeds the format-variable names (`added`, `failed`) into the key itself. The key is also propagated verbatim into every non-English locale. The matching `FormattedMessage` in `TranscriptionDetailsDialog.tsx:267-272` defines a `defaultMessage` for a message that is not referenced by id, so the `pnpm --filter desktop i18n` extraction should regenerate a proper, descriptive key like `added_words_to_your_dictionary_with_failures`.

---
Reply with `@kilocode-bot fix it` to have Kilo Code address this issue.

**WARNING:** `findEditCorrections` produces false positives for single-word dictations against an unrelated focused field. The single-token zero-overlap guard is intentionally skipped (the comment at line 70 explains this), so `insertedText: "hello"` with `fieldText: "Bo"` (a focused field that has nothing to do with the dictation) returns `["Bo"]` and the user gets prompted to add `Bo` to the dictionary. The right mitigation is to require the best-scoring window from `locateInsertedWindow` to overlap by at least one token in the multi-token case, and for the single-token case to compare the inserted token to the surrounding field context (e.g. preceding/following punctuation or a shared context token) before accepting the diff.

---
Reply with `@kilocode-bot fix it` to have Kilo Code address this issue.

**SUGGESTION:** `acceptAutoLearnProposal` discards the `{ created, failed }` return value from `createGlossaryTerms`, so a user who taps Add on the pill sees no feedback when the insert fails (e.g. transient DB error or duplicate). The result object is already typed and the `TranscriptionDetailsDialog.tsx` flow already differentiates success, partial success, and full failure toasts. Mirror that here with `failed > 0` showing the error snackbar and `failed === 0` showing the confirmation snackbar, or at least log a warning so the failure is observable.

---
Reply with `@kilocode-bot fix it` to have Kilo Code address this issue.

**SUGGESTION:** The partial-failure branch is shown with `{ mode: "success" }` even though some glossary inserts failed. The toast text does say `"(N failed)"`, but the snackbar color/icon is the success variant, which contradicts the warning tone of the text and the error-mode branch right below it. Use `mode: "warning"` here so the user actually notices the failure and can retry.

---
Reply with `@kilocode-bot fix it` to have Kilo Code address this issue.

**SUGGESTION:** `beginEditWatch` is called after a successful local paste/type but before checking whether the focused field is even the one the user is now editing. The poll reads the focused text field via `get_text_field_info`, so if the user switches focus immediately after the dictation lands (a very common post-dictation action), the watcher will silently learn corrections made in a different app or a different field. Consider storing the just-targeted app/field identifier in the snapshot and ignoring the poll result when focus has changed, or starting the watch only after a short quiescent period during which focus has not moved.

---
Reply with `@kilocode-bot fix it` to have Kilo Code address this issue.
